Christopher Columbus

The draft died down, leaving the chamber in a heavy silence. Frederick looked at the parchment, the ink shimmering with a faint, unnatural glow. He thought of the centuries he would have to watch, the friends who would turn to dust, the loneliness that stretched into infinity. The allure of eternal life was a siren song, but the cost was his humanity.

With a trembling hand, Frederick did not reach for the vial of ingredients he had carefully prepared. Instead, he reached for the candle on the altar. He held the flame to the corner of the ancient book. The parchment curled and blackened, the runes dissolving into ash. As the knowledge of eternal life vanished, so too did the weight of the decision. Frederick smiled, not with the joy of power, but with the relief of freedom. He turned and walked out of the hidden chamber, leaving the secret to the dark, choosing a mortal life filled with meaning over an endless existence devoid of connection.
